source_quotes.n_subjects: We enlisted 22 healthy, right-handed volunteers with no history of neurologic or psychiatric disorders, except those with a history of depression, who were in remission for ≥one year (Table 1). Additional exclusion criteria included the following: having close relatives with a history of seizures, a predisposition to fainting, excessive hair that could impede transducer coupling, current or planned pregnancy, presence of any implanted metallic devices, skin diseases, claustrophobia, or anxiety related to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and tattoos near the head. The participants received compensation of £40 on completion of their participation. This study was approved by the University of Nottingham Faculty of Psychology Ethics Committee (reference: F1298R) and adhered to the ethical principles outlined in the Declaration of Helsinki of 1978, as amended in 2008. Written informed consent was obtained from all participants before their participation in the study.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: The study was conducted in three phases (Fig. 1). Initially, the participants completed a 45-minute MRI session. Subsequently, the participants were pseudorandomly assigned to either the group that underwent TUS targeting the right IFC (IFC-TUS) or the group that underwent TUS targeting the right thalamus (Thal-TUS). This second step was necessary to individually plan the TUS (ie, to identify the target location on the native T1 and the optimal transducer position over the head). Finally, TUS was administered to the designated target, followed by another 45-minute MRI session (approximately 15 minutes between the TUS and the beginning of the MRI). The initial and final MRI sessions were conducted on separate days, with a minimum interval of one week between sessions.

source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: For the application of ultrasound stimulation, we used the NeuroFUS PRO TPO-203 system equipped with the four-element CTX-500-4CH transducer (manufacturer: Sonic Concepts Inc, Bothell, WA; supplier: Brainbox Ltd, Cardiff, UK; number of elements: four; radius of curvature: 63.2 mm; aperture diameter: 45 mm; steering range: 30–70 mm). We used a theta-burst TUS protocol<sup>4,12</sup> with the following parameters: fundamental frequency: 500 kHz, pulse duration: 20 milliseconds, pulse repetition interval: 200 milliseconds, pulse repetition frequency: 5 Hz, duty cycle: 10%, spatial-peak pulse-average intensity: 54.51W/cm<sup>2</sup>, and total duration: 80 seconds. These settings adhere to the safety guidelines.<sup>26,27</sup> To achieve proper coupling between the ultrasound transducer and the participant’s head, an ultrasound transmission gel was applied to both the head and the transducer face, ensuring the manual removal of any air bubbles (using a syringe). The position of the transducer was based on the outputs provided by the code we developed,<sup>25</sup> allowing us to manually hold the transducer in the correct location and orientation during all stimulations.

flags.reason: Paper states participants were 'pseudorandomly assigned' to groups; exact allocation procedure not detailed.

Domain of the 54.51 W/cm2 spatial-peak pulse-average intensity (device setting) is not explicitly stated as free-field/water vs in situ; assigned to free_field as it is listed as a fixed device parameter separate from the per-subject acoustic simulation results in Table 1.
Authors explicitly state there is no valid sham model used or available for this TUS study; no control condition was included.
